title: Compatibility surface matrix for model-ops and contractual impact assessment
creator: Maya Chen
description: Run a structured assessment of the operator-facing compatibility surface across model families and vendors, produce a matrix that maps API/format/version incompatibilities to concrete product and contract risks, and recommend mitigations and playbooks for enterprise customers to reduce migration friction. Focus areas: inference API shapes (streaming vs unary), tokenizer/token id mapping differences, embedding dimensionality and normalization, KV cache semantics, quantization/bitwidth behavior, and rollout/rollback capabilities for model variants.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical compatibility matrix exists covering at least 6 model families and 3 vendor variants
Each incompatibility is classified (break/fix/behavioral/regression) and mapped to customer-facing impact and mitigation cost estimate
Migration playbook and template SLA language drafted for sales/legal for three tiers: Hosted, Dedicated, Private
Automated compatibility test harness prototype integrated into model onboarding CI and run against two recent vendor releases
Stakeholders (Sales, Legal, Eng, Support) have reviewed and signed off on mitigation recommendations
tasks: Run compatibility scans against model artifacts (tokenizer mapping, config keys, ops) - Eng
Propose standard translation/adaptation layers for common incompatibilities - PM/Eng
Draft contractual addendum templates for model-change SLAs - PM/Legal
Instrument telemetry events to detect silent behavior changes in production - Eng/Observability
Create migration checklist for customers with Dedicated/Private deployments - PM/SE
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with Eng (runtime), Legal, and Solutions Eng. Agreed scope: 6 model families prioritized by customer usage and latency/cost sensitivity.
2026-03-05: Initial scan completed for two Llama-family forks and one M* family model; found tokenizer id remapping and embedding-dims mismatch issues that break downstream indexers.
2026-03-08: Decision to add an automated tokenizer compatibility check to onboarding CI. Diego to own prototypes; estimate 3 points of eng effort.
2026-03-10: Sales raised concern about contractual exposure for scheduled vendor patch windows; legal requested a fallback SLA clause and a two-tier credit schedule.

2026-03-13: Prototype harness ran against latest vendor nightly: detected KV-cache eviction semantic change causing 5% latency regression in 2048-seq traces; temporary mitigation: pin model variant and notify customers via feature flag.
2026-03-15: Review meeting scheduled with Support to align incident escalation paths and with Console team for telemetry surface. Next: draft playbook and add to trial runbook.
